finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: POST /hooks/test sends a server-side request to an attacker-supplied URL with no validation, allowing access to internal services and cloud metadata endpoints. Only the response status is returned, so the attacker gets a limited oracle, but the request itself, including the POST, is fully attacker-directed.

trace.note: pub router has no auth middleware
upstream status code returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: No scheme or host allowlist, no private/loopback/link-local IP blocking, no DNS-rebinding protection. Axios follows redirects by default. No authentication on the pub router (requireAdmin is applied only to admin).

verdict.reason: routes.js:20 passes req.body.callback straight to axios.post in the POST /hooks/test handler (routes.js:19) on the `pub` router, which has no auth (requireAdmin is only applied to `admin` at routes.js:12), with no URL validation anywhere; the trace's "line 5" for pub is really line 4, a trivial off-by-one.

finding.claim: SSRF via the admin diagnostics fetch endpoint: the URL comes straight from the query string with no destination validation. It is gated by an admin role check, so exploitation requires an admin session or a compromised or CSRF'd admin. Lower severity, but it still reaches internal and metadata addresses.
finding.source: req.query.url (HTTP GET query string, admin router)
finding.guards_checked: requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10) checks req.session.role === 'admin', which limits callers to admins. There is no URL scheme or host allowlist, no private IP blocking, and redirects are followed. Whether the admin router is mounted is not visible in this file.

verdict.guard_found: requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10, applied at routes.js:12) requires session role === 'admin'; no URL validation exists.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (routes.js:12-16) and there is no URL guard, but the source req.query.url at routes.js:15 is reachable only behind requireAdmin (routes.js:8,12), so it is not controllable by an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker.
